answer: Picture an agent economy as a lagoon where every new identity must post a bond before it can earn or vote. The bond stays locked for ninety days and is slashed if peers prove two identities share keys or coordinated behavior. An attacker spinning up a thousand sybils must freeze a thousand bonds, and one detected link cracks the scheme like brittle shale, burning every deposit. Faking a persona is as cheap as copying a sonnet. Keeping that much capital idle and at risk is not.
